title: Safer eating, allergies and choking
description: Allergies, weaning, preventing choking and food poisoning at mealtimes. Based on section 3 of the EYFS statutory framework.

questions.prompt: What must the provider find out before a child is admitted to the setting?

options.text: Any special dietary requirements, preferences, food allergies and intolerances, and any special health requirements
Only the child's favourite foods
Only whether the child eats meat
Nothing until the child's first meal

questions.explanation: Before a child is admitted, the provider must obtain information about special dietary requirements, preferences, food allergies and intolerances, and special health requirements. It must be shared with all staff who prepare and handle food.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: At snack time, who is responsible for checking that the food and drink meets each child's needs?

options.text: Whoever the setting has made clear is responsible at that mealtime or snack time
Whoever happens to be nearest
The child
Nobody, if the menu was agreed last term

questions.explanation: At each mealtime and snack time, providers must be clear about who is responsible for checking that the food and drink meets all the requirements for each child.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Children can develop allergies at any time, especially when solid foods are first introduced. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. All staff must know that children can develop allergies at any time, especially during the introduction of solid foods, which is sometimes called weaning.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: How should a setting manage a child's known allergy?

options.text: Develop an allergy action plan with parents and carers, and with health professionals where appropriate, keep it up to date and share it with all staff
Keep it in the manager's head
Ask the child to avoid the food themselves
Wait for a reaction before making a plan

questions.explanation: Providers must have ongoing discussions with parents and carers, and where appropriate health professionals, to develop allergy action plans. The plans must be kept up to date and shared with all staff.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: You can decide what textures a child can eat by their age alone. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Providers must talk with parents and carers about the stage the child is at with solid foods, including the textures they know. Assumptions must not be made based on age.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: What must providers do when preparing food for babies and young children?

options.text: Prepare food in a way that prevents choking
Offer the same size pieces to every child
Leave preparation to the child's parents
Only worry about choking for babies

questions.explanation: Providers must prepare food in a way to prevent choking. The government's food safety guidance for early years providers explains what to avoid and how to reduce the risk.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers
Food safety: help for early years providers (GOV.UK)

questions.prompt: Where must a member of staff be while children are eating?

options.text: Children must always be within sight and hearing of a member of staff
In the next room, listening for noise
Anywhere in the building
Only in the room if a child is under one

questions.explanation: Children must always be within sight and hearing of a member of staff while eating. Where possible, sit facing the children.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: A child who is choking will always make a loud noise. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Choking can be completely silent, so staff must stay alert to a child who may be starting to choke.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: A child needed help after choking on a piece of food. What should the setting do afterwards?

options.text: Record where and how the child choked and make sure parents and carers know
Nothing, as the child is fine now
Tell only the manager
Remove the child from lunch for a week

questions.explanation: When a choking incident needs intervention, providers should record details of where and how it happened and make sure parents and carers are aware. Records should be reviewed from time to time to spot trends.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: While children are eating, who should always be in the room?

options.text: A member of staff with a valid paediatric first aid certificate
The cook
A parent volunteer
The manager, if they are free

questions.explanation: Whilst children are eating there should always be a member of staff in the room with a valid paediatric first aid certificate for a full course.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Two children become ill with food poisoning after a meal at the setting. What must the registered provider do?

options.text: Tell Ofsted as soon as reasonably practicable, and within 14 days
Nothing, if the children get better
Tell Ofsted only after the next inspection
Tell the other parents but nobody else

questions.explanation: Registered providers must notify Ofsted (or the childminder agency) of any food poisoning affecting two or more children cared for on the premises, as soon as is reasonably practicable and in any event within 14 days.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: A new child, Sam, is about to start. His mum mentions he has a nut allergy and the doctor gave him an action plan.

steps.text: What should the setting do before Sam's first day?

choices.text: Get the allergy information and plan from Sam's parents, share it with all staff who prepare and handle food, and agree who checks his food
choices.feedback: Yes. This must happen before a child is admitted.
The information must be shared with all staff who prepare and handle food.

choices.text: Ask the parents to bring a note on his first day
choices.feedback: The setting needs the information before he is admitted, not after.

steps.text: On Sam's third day another child shares a snack that might contain nuts. Sam has not eaten any. What next?

choices.text: Move the snack, check what Sam may have eaten, and follow his allergy action plan if you see any symptoms
choices.feedback: Right. Stay close and follow the plan.

choices.text: Do nothing, since Sam has not eaten any
choices.feedback: Act now to stop the sharing. Sitting facing the children helps you prevent food sharing.

choices.text: Wait until the end of the day to mention it
choices.feedback: Act straight away and follow the action plan if symptoms appear.

questions.explanation: Get the child's allergy information and action plan before they are admitted, share it with all staff, and prevent food sharing at mealtimes.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: At lunch, Jo, aged 2, goes quiet and looks upset. There was no cough or noise. You are busy at the other table.

choices.text: Go to Jo straight away and check, because choking can be silent
choices.feedback: Right. Silence does not mean a child is fine.
Choking can be completely silent. Check straight away.

choices.text: Wait to see if Jo makes a noise
choices.feedback: Children can choke without any noise. Go to them at once.

questions.explanation: Choking can be completely silent, so staff must be within sight and hearing and ready to act. A trained first aider should be in the room while children eat.
